subject: Social Habits
title: Our community helpers
objectives: Children will name community helpers and what they do.
content: Teachers and nurses, drivers, farmers and market sellers, and thanking helpers.
teachingActivities: Use local helpers children know (the nurse at the clinic, the bus driver, the market seller, the farmer, the gateman); invite a helper to visit if possible; keep role play positive; avoid gender stereotypes about jobs; use real objects such as a stethoscope toy.
learnerActivities: Name community helpers and what they do and say thank you to a helper.
resources: Toy vegetables and a play market
assessment: Observe whether each child names two helpers and says thank you to a helper.
expectedOutcomes: Names two or more community helpers.
Says thank you to a helper.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: people and jobs

lessons.title: Teachers and nurses
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name teachers and nurses and say how they help.
successCriteria: Names a teacher and a nurse
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can cooperate and show respect.
resources: Pictures of a teacher and a nurse
lessons.starter: Show a picture of a nurse and say "A nurse helps us when we are sick."
teacherActivities: Show pictures of a teacher and a nurse and say what they do.
Show a toy medical kit and name each item.
Let children be nurse and patient with a doll.
Say "Thank you, nurse. Thank you, teacher."
learnerActivities: Children look and repeat the job.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of a teacher and a nurse and say what they do. Children: Children look and repeat the job.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a toy medical kit and name each item. Children: Children touch and name items.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children be nurse and patient with a doll. Children: Child plays nurse or patient.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Thank you, nurse. Thank you, teacher." Children: Children say thank you.

practical.title: Nurse role play
practical.safety: Use only a toy kit with no real medicines or sharp items. Keep play gentle and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Play together and name the job.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how a nurse helps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who helps us when we are sick?

expectedOutcomes: Names a teacher and a nurse
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about the nurse and teacher your child knows.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name teachers and nurses and say how they help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Helpers, helpers, helpers in our town.

lessons.title: Drivers and farmers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name drivers and farmers and say how they help.
successCriteria: Names a driver and a farmer
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can cooperate and show respect.
resources: Pictures of a bus driver and a farmer
lessons.starter: Show a toy bus and say "The driver takes people to school and work."
teacherActivities: Show a picture of a driver and say what the driver does.
Show a picture of a farmer and say what the farmer grows.
Let children drive a toy bus and plant toy seeds.
Say "Thank you, driver. Thank you, farmer."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture of a driver and say what the driver does. Children: Children look and repeat.
Step 2. Teacher: Show a picture of a farmer and say what the farmer grows. Children: Children name a food.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children drive a toy bus and plant toy seeds. Children: Child plays driver or farmer.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Thank you, driver. Thank you, farmer." Children: Children say thank you.

practical.title: Driver and farmer play
practical.safety: Use only toys and keep movement slow and safe. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play together and name the job.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say where the food comes from.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names a driver and a farmer
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about the drivers and farmers you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name drivers and farmers and say how they help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The market seller
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play at a market and use manners with the seller.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can cooperate and show respect.
lessons.starter: Set up a play market and say "The seller helps us get food. We say please and thank you."
teacherActivities: Show how to ask the seller for a tomato.
Let children buy and sell toy food.
Swap roles so everyone has a go.
learnerActivities: Child says please and thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to ask the seller for a tomato. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children buy and sell toy food. Children: Child buys or sells.
Step 3. Teacher: Remind children of manners. Children: Child says please and thank you.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles so everyone has a go. Children: Child swaps and plays again.

practical.title: Market play
practical.safety: Use only toy food and tokens too large to swallow. Supervise swapping and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Be the seller while the child is the buyer.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the seller and give change with tokens.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the market and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Visit a market with your child and greet the seller.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play at a market and use manners with the seller" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Thanking helpers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will make a thank-you card for a community helper.
successCriteria: Makes a card with marks or drawing
Says thank you to a helper
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can cooperate and show respect.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we make a card to say thank you to a helper."
teacherActivities: Show a sample card and say who it is for.
Let each child choose a helper and draw or mark a card.
Help each child add their name.
Deliver the cards to the helpers or display them.
learnerActivities: Child gives or points to the card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a sample card and say who it is for. Children: Children look and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child choose a helper and draw or mark a card. Children: Child makes a card.
Step 3. Teacher: Help each child add their name. Children: Child adds a mark.
Step 4. Teacher: Deliver the cards to the helpers or display them. Children: Child gives or points to the card.

practical.title: Thank-you cards
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and keep stickers away from mouths. Deliver cards with adult supervision.

differentiation.support: Draw together and choose the helper.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what the helper does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says thank you to a helper
lessons.conclusion: Hold the cards up and say "Thank you, helpers."
lessons.homeConnection: Say thank you to helpers in your neighbourhood.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a thank-you card for a community helper" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 helpers check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child talks about helpers.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can cooperate and show respect.
lessons.starter: Sing the helper song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: nurse, market and card.
At each station ask "Who is the helper?"
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: nurse, market and card. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Who is the helper?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Helper stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use toys and safe materials only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name three helpers.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names community helpers; says what they do; plays a helper role; says thank you.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child talks about helpers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
